paper_title: Artificial intelligence links CT images to pathologic features and survival outcomes of renal masses
prediction_task: Renal mass classification and survival prediction from multi-phase CT images

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Three-phase model achieves best performance but authors haven't shown what each phase contributes. Which radiological phenotypes in each phase correlate with predictions?
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added phase-specific contribution analysis and CAM visualization per phase.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Only one slice with maximum tumour extracted per CT — ignores spatial heterogeneity. Should test with smaller tumour slice. nnUNet segmentation may fail for difficult images from TCIA.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added multi-slice analysis and segmentation failure rate reporting.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: After segmentation, why not focus on kidney areas by masking background? Benign CAM in Figure C shows attention paid to background areas. Why not include segmentation results as additional input?
Intra-observer variability of three pathologists in revaluating tumour subtypes not reported. Arterial phase segmentation labelled by only one radiologist — annotation bias.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added inter-rater agreement and second reader validation.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Code available but trained weights not shared. Checked code in repository — seems reasonable but can't run without pre-trained model.

reviewer_strengths.text: Methodology is sound, experiments support conclusions. Multi-centre CT dataset with potential association to survival and gene mutation.
